meta.title: Independent cold-case review
meta.author: Claude (AI analyst), independent review requested by the project owner
meta.disclaimer: AI analysis is not evidence. Grades describe how well the archive's sources support an item, from provenance and independence, not truth. Nothing here identifies an offender. Edit this file to correct the analysis; record agreement or disagreement on the board.
meta.method: Evidence-first: the 1997 contemporaneous articles, the official GBI pages and the 2004 GBI chronology were read before any suspect narrative. Claims are traced to their earliest available lineage; repeated renditions of one lineage count once.

lineages.label: 1997 Forsyth County News contemporaneous reporting (sheriff, GBI and family quotes)
GBI investigative chronology released 2004 (FCN timeline, AccessNorthGa, Dawson News clipping and 2016 blog are renditions of this ONE lineage)
Official GBI web pages 2017+ (case page, 20-year release, Levi's Call page)
levifrady.com 2016-2020 (single author; many unnamed sources; some primary documents reproduced)
Later newspaper/TV retrospectives 2000-2026 (officials quoted years later)
1997 AJC reporting cited by the blog but not held by the archive

gradeScale.meaning: Official record or multiple independent contemporaneous lineages agree; no credible conflict.
Two independent lineages, or an official statement plus a consistent contemporaneous account.
One credible lineage (often the GBI chronology) with no conflict, or several with minor variance.
Plausible on one weak or indirect lineage; important limitations.
Asserted by an identifiable but interested, hostile or unverified party.
Anonymous, hearsay or retrospective with no traceable basis.

overview.headline: An 11-year-old boy riding his bicycle home at dusk on a rural Forsyth County road disappeared within a window of roughly 25 minutes; he was found shot about 19 hours later in a state forest roughly 15–22 road miles away. Nobody has been charged.
paragraphs: On Wednesday 22 October 1997 Levi Frady rode the school bus home and was alone at his Burruss Mill Road home after about 4:12 p.m.; his mother was at work in Alpharetta and his twin sister Laci was still at school. He phoned his mother, was told to be home by 6:30, and spent the afternoon cycling between two friends' homes. He left his book bag on friend #2's patio when that family went out to eat at about 5:45–6:00.

At 6:38 he phoned home from a third residence and told Laci he did not want to ride home because it was getting dark and he was afraid of dogs on the route. He set off at about 6:45–6:50 by the Little Mill Road route to avoid the dogs. A resident saw him on Little Mill Road at 6:50, heading toward friend #2's house, with a small black dog following. Sunset was about 6:55 p.m. EDT and civil dusk about 7:20 (computed, not sourced).

Between 6:52 and 7:00 a lost motorist spoke to a man who did not answer and walked into the woods at a driveway a few hundred feet from where the bicycle was later found; she saw no bicycle. Between 7:00 and 7:15 Laci, searching by car with her mother, saw a bicycle like Levi's lying at a driveway on Little Mill Road about half a mile from home. If both accounts are accurate, the bicycle reached the roadside between about 6:52 and 7:15, and that is the best estimate of when Levi was taken.

His mother checked friend #1's house at about 7:30 and was told Levi had left to eat with another family. That family was out (an 8:01 Kmart check is reported). Believing he was staying at a friend's, she went to sleep, searched by car at about 2 a.m., and filed a missing-person report at 8 a.m. Before the report, the bicycle had been moved twice: by a resident's children into the ditch at 6:45 a.m., and by relatives who took it to the mother's house and then returned it.

At about 2 p.m. on 23 October, the opening day of rifle deer season, three Gilmer County hunters found Levi's body in Dawson Forest Wildlife Management Area near the abandoned Lockheed site. The sheriff said he was killed at that scene ('It all happened here'). Later accounts say he was shot three times, and a later sheriff mentioned 'a couple of shell casings'. The official interval for the shooting runs from 6 p.m. on the 22nd to 2:30 p.m. on the 23rd. The archive cannot say whether he was killed that evening or the next morning.

Investigators publicly sought two possible witnesses. One was a man walking Little Mill Road at about 6:30 p.m. The other was a man in Dawson Forest with a 1980–85 medium-blue Toyota 2WD pickup with a white camper shell, seen at about 10 a.m. on the 23rd. They have sought both since 1997. Three agencies shared the case, and their working relationship was documented as strained. Later suspect narratives, mainly from one blog, rest on anonymous sources and a hostile party's statement. No official source has adopted them.

observations.title: The abduction window is about 6:50–7:15 p.m., not '6–7 p.m.'
observations.detail: The 6:50 sighting on Little Mill Road, the motorist seeing no bicycle at 6:52–7:00 and Laci's bicycle sighting at 7:00–7:15 bracket the event to roughly 25 minutes at sunset. The GBI's public 'before the sun went down, 6–7 p.m.' is broader and earlier than its own chronology. A narrow window on a 'well-traveled' road makes passing drivers the most valuable possible witnesses.

observations.title: When Levi was killed is the most important unknown
observations.detail: The official shooting window runs from 6 p.m. on the 22nd to 2:30 p.m. on the 23rd. Investigators have kept seeking a man seen in Dawson Forest at about 10 a.m. on the 23rd, 15 hours after the abduction. That makes most sense if they could not rule out Levi being alive, or the offender being present, that morning. The 23rd was the opening day of rifle season, when gunfire would go unnoticed. Evening killing and overnight custody imply different offenders and motives. The autopsy (stomach contents set against a skipped dinner, rigor, lividity, wetness after rain) is the answer, and the archive does not hold it.

observations.title: The bicycle's 'found location' is a reconstruction after at least three handlings
observations.detail: At 5:15 a.m. the bicycle was at the edge of a driveway. Children moved it into the ditch at 6:45. Relatives took it to the mother's house and then put it back before police arrived. The 1997 press (Laci found it; Laci and her mother found it) does not reflect any of this; the GBI chronology first did in 2004. The placement (lying at a driveway edge, not hidden) best fits a bicycle dropped at the point of encounter. The blog's 'wiped clean' claim is anonymous, and the handling plus the reported drizzle are mundane explanations for missing prints.

observations.title: He said he did not want to ride home in the dark
observations.detail: At 6:38 Levi said he was afraid of the dark and of dogs, and he chose a different route. A ride offered by a familiar adult would have been welcome, which fits his mother's belief that he would not get into a stranger's car. This raises the plausibility of a known or locally familiar driver without pointing to anyone.

observations.title: The man at the driveway (6:52–7:00) is the closest observation to the abduction, and he is not one of the sought witnesses
observations.detail: The lost motorist's man was 35–60, with scraggly grayish-black or light-brown hair, jeans, and a light shirt with rolled sleeves. He ignored her and walked into the woods at a driveway a few hundred feet from the bicycle site. Witness 1 was seen at 6:30 and is described as late 50s, gray beard, blue cap, stooped. The records held never say whether the driveway man was identified (perhaps a resident at his own driveway) or simply dropped.

observations.title: The delay in reporting has a documented, mundane explanation
observations.detail: At 7:30 friend #1's parents told the mother that Levi had left to eat with another family. That family really was out (Kmart, 8:01), and Levi had an invitation and money. Her account that she believed he was staying at a friend's is consistent from 1997 to 2004. The 8 a.m. report is not, on this record, an anomaly that needs a sinister explanation.

observations.title: 'It all happened here': the shooting was at the Dawson scene
observations.detail: Sheriff Carlisle said this on 24 October 1997, and Paxton's 'couple of shell casings' (2002) fits a shooting at the scene. The 2007 line that casings were found with the bicycle in the Little Mill ditch conflicts with both and is best treated as a retelling error. Hendrix's 'a crime occurred in this county' is most simply the abduction itself, which is a crime in Forsyth. The blog reads it as a sign Levi died before reaching Dawson, which overreads it.

observations.title: The father's avoidance has a documented reason, and the GBI later all but excluded him
observations.detail: Milton Frady had a 1995 failure-to-appear bench warrant and feared arrest at the funeral. He surrendered on 29 October, was interviewed with counsel, and by 19 December the GBI said he had 'pretty much been ruled out'. His alibi for the evening rests on his own mother, which is an interested source, but nothing held contradicts it.

observations.title: The Tallant/Samples narrative has little evidentiary weight so far
observations.detail: Its core is a statement made in 2013, during a stabbing investigation, by a man with a documented psychiatric history and a violent dispute with the accused ('long gun … same one they shot Levi Frady with'), with no stated basis of knowledge. Added to it are one anonymous 'they were friends' claim and an uncorroborated 2020 warrant report. A 2026-10-29 web search found no independent report of the warrant. The 1998 inmate in the Hendrix letter is unlikely to be Samples: Samples was awaiting trial or out on bond in 1998, and Hendrix described the inmate as his informant from Fulton County years earlier. The decisive test is a ballistic comparison, which only the GBI can run.

observations.title: Modern forensic options are the most realistic route to resolution
observations.detail: In 2004 the GBI said the evidence was 'painstakingly preserved' and being reviewed for resubmission; the bicycle was in GBI evidence in Cleveland. Casings and projectiles can be compared through NIBIN. Clothing, a sexual-assault kit if one exists, fingernail scrapings and bicycle grips can be tested with touch/Y-STR DNA and probabilistic genotyping, then forensic genetic genealogy if a usable male profile results. Most of this was unavailable or immature in 1997, and all of it is in agency custody.

evidence.whatWeKnow: 'One or more gunshot wounds' (1997); 'shot three times' (later). Wound sites, range, trajectory, sequence, time-of-death indicators and sexual-assault findings are not public.
evidence.custodian: GBI Medical Examiner / Division of Forensic Sciences; Dawson County coroner
evidence.forensicOpportunity: Time-of-death reassessment (stomach contents vs last meal, lividity, rigor, insects, wetness). Wound sequence tests the anonymous 'not fired at same time/place' claim.

evidence.whatWeKnow: Count, caliber and weapon class not public. 'A couple' set against three shots may mean a casing was missed, a manually operated weapon, or loose wording.
evidence.forensicOpportunity: NIBIN entry and correlation; comparison with any weapon seized since (tests the 'long gun' claim).
Rifling characteristics narrow the weapon class; comparison with any test-fired weapon.

evidence.status: In GBI evidence at Cleveland as of Oct 2004 (AJC caption)
evidence.whatWeKnow: Handled by the residents' children, relatives (taken to the mother's house and returned) and then officers. 'No prints / wiped clean' is anonymous (blog). Light rain/drizzle was reported.
evidence.forensicOpportunity: Touch DNA on grips, seat and brake levers with probabilistic genotyping, using elimination samples from known handlers. Low but non-zero yield.

evidence.item: Book bag left on friend #2's patio
evidence.whatWeKnow: Left about 5:45–6:00. Whether, when and by whom it was recovered is never stated.
evidence.forensicOpportunity: Not forensic. It establishes whether Levi went back for it after 6:50, and so his route.

evidence.whatWeKnow: 'He was clothed' (Carlisle). Whether every reported item was present was not disclosed.
evidence.forensicOpportunity: Trace and touch DNA, fibers, gunshot residue pattern (range of fire).

evidence.whatWeKnow: Officials withheld it as 'guilty knowledge'. Blog hearsay (funeral home) and an anonymous denial (an officer at the autopsy) conflict.
evidence.forensicOpportunity: If a kit or swabs exist: Y-STR / autosomal retest, then FIGG if a male profile results.

evidence.item: Crime-scene photographs, sketch and search records
evidence.whatWeKnow: The scene was later clear-cut, so these are now the only record of it. The blog describes the body face up in a rain-filled pit about 300 yards from the Etowah River (unsourced).
evidence.forensicOpportunity: Reconstruct body position, approach route and vehicle access with 1990s aerials.

evidence.item: Composite sketches (Nov 5 pair, third roadblock sketch, Witness 1, Witness 2)
evidence.status: Two published; others resolved or unreleased
evidence.whatWeKnow: Nov 5 pair: one man identified by tag. Third: identified and interviewed. Witness 1 and Witness 2 still sought in 2026.
evidence.forensicOpportunity: Re-release with the specific vehicle description; Georgia DOR historical registrations for 1980–85 Toyota 2WD pickups (if retained).

evidence.item: Telephone records (6:38 call; 7:02 call; Milton's evening calls)
evidence.whatWeKnow: The 6:38 call came from a third residence. Sarah said Milton called the children's home on the night of the 22nd and was told Levi was at a neighbor's.
evidence.custodian: GBI file (1997 subpoenaed LUDs, if obtained)
evidence.forensicOpportunity: Fixes the times of the last contact and tests the father's alibi call.

evidence.item: Investigative file (66 volumes, 500+ leads, 20+ polygraphs, search warrant for the mother's home)
evidence.status: Exists; exempt while the case is open
evidence.forensicOpportunity: A file review by a fresh team is itself the best available 'test'.

evidence.item: Tallant's tan Dodge van 'taken by law enforcement' (1997)
evidence.forensicOpportunity: If true, impound or search records exist.

people.name: Levi Frady
people.whyTheyMatter: Victimology: careful of strangers per his mother; afraid of the dark and of dogs; carried money that day; a regular rider of these routes.

people.name: Marilyn Parkman (also Weaver / Hamby in later sources)
people.role: Mother; source of most of the family chronology
people.whyTheyMatter: Her account anchors the 4:12, 6:38, 7:00–7:34 and 2 a.m. entries and is consistent from 1997 to 2004.
people.caution: Being a primary source makes her central to the record. It does not make her a suspect. The 1997 investigation examined everyone close to the family as a matter of routine.

people.name: Laci Frady
people.whyTheyMatter: Possible bicycle sighting at 7:00–7:15 (pivotal); took the 6:38 and 7:02 calls. Now an adult, she is the best surviving witness to the evening.
people.caution: Child witness; account first reported via others.

people.name: Milton Frady
people.whyTheyMatter: Fugitive on a 1995 warrant at the time; interviewed 29 Oct; 'pretty much ruled out' (Dec 1997).
people.caution: The 1997 press framed his absence speculatively; it has a documented mundane reason.

people.name: Sarah (Sara) Frady
people.whyTheyMatter: Gave Milton's alibi (porch 5:15, calls that night and the next morning). Independently corroborates the 7:02 call.

people.name: Dorsey Hamby
people.whyTheyMatter: Per the 2004 chronology, the 'grandfather' and relatives found the bicycle and moved it.
people.caution: Handling evidence before police arrived is common family behavior in a search and does not imply intent.

people.name: Janice Hamby
people.whyTheyMatter: Letters and press statements 1997–2007; gave '6–6:30' for the ride home.
people.caution: Her basis of knowledge for times is unknown.

people.name: Tim Tatum
people.whyTheyMatter: Arrived at the driveway at 7:00–7:15 per the chronology; at work at 9:30 the next morning.
people.caution: The only adverse item is an anonymous 2014 claim (RUMOR). Employer records could exclude it.

people.name: Friend #1 (blog names Roman Martinez)
people.whyTheyMatter: Officially the last person known to have seen Levi; can describe his departure and direction.
people.caution: The identity rests on the blog alone.

people.name: Unnamed neighborhood witnesses
people.role: 6:50 resident; lost motorist; Bronco driver; driveway residents and children; hunter
people.whyTheyMatter: They define the abduction window and the morning-after observation.
people.caution: Identities are held by the GBI; do not guess.

people.name: Witness 1 and Witness 2
people.whyTheyMatter: Witness 1: Little Mill Road walker, 6:30. Witness 2: Toyota/camper man in Dawson Forest, about 10 a.m. Oct 23.
people.caution: The GBI expressly calls them possible witnesses, not suspects.

people.name: Investigators
people.role: Carlisle (Dawson Sheriff), Hallman / Cagle / Attaway (GBI), Hendrix / Born (Forsyth), Tanner, Branson (crime-scene tech), Paxton
people.whyTheyMatter: Their public statements are the official layer of the record; several are reachable for interviews.
people.caution: Agency friction is documented; read each account with its institutional perspective in mind.

people.name: Marshall Tallant and Tommy Albert Samples
people.whyTheyMatter: Subject of an unverified accusation; see H-06.
people.caution: No official source names either man as a suspect. Listed separately so that placement implies nothing.

people.name: Kimberly Boim
people.whyTheyMatter: The single largest secondary source; reproduced primary documents (letters, court records, video).
people.caution: One author; many anonymous sources; interpretive headlines.

locations.notes: 'Less than a mile' from the bicycle site (GBI); the bicycle was 'about half a mile' (1997, 2004) or 'about a mile' (29 Oct 1997) away.

locations.name: Friend #1's home, Noah Road
locations.notes: Levi left from here at about 6:45–6:50.

locations.name: Friend #2's home (road not stated)
locations.role: Book bag left on patio; family out 5:45 to after 8:01
locations.notes: Levi was heading in this direction at 6:50.

locations.name: Picklesimer Road
locations.role: The route with dogs, avoided at 6:45

locations.name: Little Mill Road bicycle site (a resident's driveway)
locations.notes: Bicycle at the driveway edge by 5:15 a.m., possibly by 7:15 p.m. The motorist's man entered the woods a few hundred feet away. A 'well-traveled two-lane road between Hwys 306 and 369'.

contradictions.title: When was Levi killed — the evening of the 22nd or the morning of the 23rd?
versions: Official window: 6 p.m. Oct 22 – 2:30 p.m. Oct 23 (FCN, Oct 31 1997)
Investigators: contact before sundown (6–7 p.m.)
Witness 2 sought for a 10 a.m. Oct 23 sighting in Dawson Forest
contradictions.assessment: Unresolved and the most consequential gap. The archive has no medical time-of-death evidence.
contradictions.whatResolves: Autopsy findings; scene photographs (rain, lividity); hunters' accounts of gunfire on the morning of the opener.

contradictions.title: Bicycle: who found it, where, when, and how many times it was moved
versions: 1997: Laci found it in a ditch about half a mile from home (26 Oct)
1997: Laci and her mother found it about a mile from home (29 Oct)
2004 GBI: seen by Laci 7–7:15 p.m.; residents 5:15 and 6:00; children moved it 6:45; grandfather and relatives took it home and returned it 7:50
contradictions.assessment: The 2004 sequence is the most detailed and comes from investigators, so it is preferred. The 1997 accounts are the family's simplified public version, most likely given after the bicycle was put back. 'Moved' is documented; 'wiped' is anonymous.
contradictions.whatResolves: Original GBI chronology; AJC 24 Oct and 9 Nov 1997; the residents' statements.

contradictions.title: What happened between 6:50 and 7:15, and where was Levi going?
versions: 6:50: heading toward friend #2's home (book bag there; family away)
Family letter: riding home on Little Mill Road 6:00–6:30
Motorist: man entering the woods at a driveway near the bicycle site, about 6:52–7:00
contradictions.assessment: The direction at 6:50 and the book bag's whereabouts are unresolved. The motorist's man's identification status is unknown.
contradictions.whatResolves: Book bag recovery; GIS of the houses relative to the bicycle site; identity of the motorist and of the driveway man.

contradictions.title: Wounds, shots and weapon
versions: 'One or more gunshot wounds' (1997)
'Gunshot blast' (editorial)
Three shots (2004 GBI chronology and later)
2 head + 1 upper body, 'not same time or location' (blog, anonymous 2014)
1 head + 2 chest (2007 forum, unsourced)
'A couple of shell casings' (2002)
'Long gun' (Samples, 2013)
'Execution-style' (2002 reporter characterization)
contradictions.assessment: The count of three is probable; the distribution, sequence and weapon class are unknown. The 'execution-style' label is a reporter's characterization, not a finding.

biasAudit.observation: Within 48 hours Carlisle reassured parents that 'the victim usually knows the perpetrator'. Such a public framing can steer early effort toward the family circle, and the warrant for the mother's home and the polygraphs fit that early focus.

Documented friction: Forsyth was asked to leave the scene, photographs and polygraph results were not shared, and GBI and Dawson declined the 2000 task force. Leads sent to Forsyth (inmate weapon claims) may not have been integrated.
Investigators gave a public '6–7 p.m., before sundown' window while their own chronology puts the last sighting at 6:50, near sunset. Public appeals may have targeted the wrong half-hour.
The FCN wrote of Milton's 'conspicuous absence … continues to fuel speculation' before he was interviewed. That is speculative framing of a fugitive-warrant issue.
Distances grow from 15 to 22 miles, casings migrate to the bicycle ditch (2007), 'execution-style' enters (2002), and 'found the following morning' appears (blog). These are classic retelling drift.

The headline 'GBI timeline confirms bicycle moved by family members before reported missing' omits that children moved it first. The Hendrix letter is quoted with an inserted negation. The task-force scandal is tied to the murder only by calendar proximity ('three days later'). These are interpretive framings and transcription discrepancies, not proof of deception.

Family-sourced details first appear in 2014 interviews 17 years later ('in the shower'; Tatum in the forest; sexual-abuse hearsay). Memory decay, grief and intra-family conflict can all shape such details.
A drug-era narrative ('sex, drugs and the murder') and local reputations attach to people by association. Drug and criminal histories are not evidence of this crime.

151 of 159 claims carry MEDIUM confidence, so the registers cannot tell established facts from rumor. Effort concentrated on peripheral chronology (Levi's Call launch date, funeral date, task-force releases) rather than the abduction window, time of death and forensics. 'Key people' is ranked by mention count, which surfaces heavily covered names.
Risk of over-reading the 2004 chronology because it is the most detailed source. It is a retrospective summary by one agency, and its details cannot be checked against the underlying statements.

provenance.claim: Detailed Oct 22–23 chronology (sightings, calls, bicycle handling)
provenance.dependentRenditions: FCN 7 Nov 2004; AccessNorthGa (captured 31 Oct 2004); Dawson News & Advertiser clipping; levifrady.com 2016
provenance.note: Four renditions count as one source. They differ slightly (the AccessNorthGa 7:50 entry lacks the 'return' clause).
Contradicted by nothing and corroborated by nothing. In Nov 1997 Hallman declined to confirm fingerprint reports.

provenance.claim: Shot twice in the head and once in the body, at different times and places
provenance.note: Conflicts with an unsourced 2007 forum version. RUMOR until the autopsy is seen.

provenance.earliestSource: FCN 9 Nov 1997 (Witness 2 caption); 2002 FCN caption; GBI pages

provenance.claim: Laci saw the bicycle on Wednesday night
provenance.note: Possibly two lineages if the AJC 1997 version is independent of the investigators. Obtain it.

overstated: The blog-originated Tallant/Samples narrative has person, evidence and event records that look structurally like core evidence. Its weight is ALLEGED/RUMOR, and nothing in the registers says so beyond notes.
The 2007 'casings in the ditch' statement sits as a co-equal version in EVD-0145…, with no note that it conflicts with official 1997 and 2002 statements.
Hendrix's 'a crime occurred in this county' risks being read (as the blog does) as evidence of a Forsyth killing, when it most simply means the abduction.
understated: The roughly 25-minute abduction window (6:50–7:15) that falls out of three independent observations.
That the time of death is entirely open, and that Witness 2's morning timing implies investigators never closed it.
The mundane, documented explanation for the delayed report (the 7:30 misinformation).
The bicycle being in GBI custody (2004) and the evidence being 'painstakingly preserved', which are the basis for realistic forensic opportunities.
The lost motorist's man and the book bag, both absent from any question list.
organizedPoorly: Confidence is flat: 151 of 159 claims are MEDIUM, so a human cannot see what is established.
master_timeline.md is ordered by ingestion batch, not chronology, and repeats events.
10_THEORIES is empty, and there is no competing-hypothesis layer anywhere.

The contradiction register (5 rows) is dominated by peripheral conflicts (funeral date, letter date, warrant wording). The case-critical conflicts (time of death, wounds, sketch accounting) are missing.
The research queue's P0/P1 effort went to bookkeeping targets rather than the questions that could change the model.
Lineage independence is described in prose notes but never counted, so repeated renditions look like corroboration on the board.
